D6·vha4 — 2026-09-15
chose: 2.2 measurement protocol, pre-registered before any label exists. CORPUS (snapshot outside the repo at ~/IO/bench-cells/tune-eval-2.2, local git 0ae9e72, manifest sha256 2c4bf41d…, rubric sha256 44727e8d…): REGRESSION split = the 9 smoke/calib bench cells with records (visible when 2.1 was designed — rediscovery only, never counted toward trust); VALIDATION split = round-1 rep-1 claude-sofar, codex-sofar, cursor-sofar (S1–S10 complete, unseen); OPERATOR split = this repo's 56 initiatives, events strictly before 01M2K1JCAKZT77FM8HEFP3HB0Z (distinct project, real sessions). LABELS: blind subagent labelers who may not read tune.ts, signals.ts, their tests, SPEC or the self-improve record, nor run sofar; they label semantic failure instances (duplicate_registration, record_correction, stall, formatter_config, mcp_rejection, sofar_cli_failure) from transcripts plus the snapshot, loss/benign/ambiguous, evidence by event id; label files are hashed into the record BEFORE replay. REPLAY: detect() bundled from b219616, rows=[] (no capture-era rows exist in any unit), signals from each unit's own settings. SCORING: finding↔label by shared event id and mapped type; TP = matches a loss; FP = matches only benign or nothing; ambiguous-only excluded and counted; FN = loss with record events in a unit where the detector ran and no finding shares an id; loss with no record event = FN-untraceable, reported apart (two recalls); loss in a unit where the detector is UNKNOWN = unobserved, never FN. COVERAGE VIOLATION = a detector prints a number on a unit whose corpus cannot contain its source while labels show ≥1 loss of its type. GATE: TRUSTED for 2.3 iff on validation ∪ operator TP+FP ≥ 5, precision ≥ 0.80, Wilson 95% lower bound ≥ 0.50, and no coverage violation on any split; otherwise UNTRUSTED naming the failing clause (insufficient evidence is not failure).
over: Scoring detectors by rediscovering the smoke preview rows (audit S3: regression, not validation); labeling with the detector's own rule or after seeing its output; committing bench-cell logs and labels into sofar's pushed git; a single pooled score across detectors and splits; a gate on recall.
because: Audit S3 asks for held-out logs from distinct sessions/projects, negative and unknown-coverage cases, frozen labels, per-detector counts. Labels must be semantic (a correction that was a change of mind is not a loss) or precision is tautological for event-type detectors, and they must come from transcripts or recall can only find what the detector's own rule finds (e.g. calib-1's biome.json edit left 0 file_touched events). Precision gates, not recall, because 2.3 turns findings into suggestions and a false alert costs trust; recall is reported so blind spots stay visible. The corpus stays out of sofar's git because round 1 is live and bench content is unpublished; hashes in the record make any later edit detectable. No corpus has capture-era rows or ok fields, so tool_failure / mcp_rejections / bookkeeping_share / injection_bytes cannot be validated here and stay untrusted by construction.
